$comment: The weight contract and the reference corpus it is calibrated against. This file is the single source: runtime/weight.mjs reads it for the composer and runtime/gates/page_gates.py reads it for the gates, so a change to a floor moves the page and the finding together. Every number under byFill is a floor, never a ceiling - the ceiling on prose is the WORDS gate. Everything under `reference` is measured by evals/corpus/measure_corpus.py against 670 published client PDFs from twelve firms; evals/corpus/README.md says what was measured and what it cost.

keys.pageWords: words in the page BODY - the title band, source and notes do not count
keys.columnFill: share of its own height the side column must reach
keys.plotSpan: share of the exhibit frame the marks must span
keys.pointWords: mean words per point in a side column
keys.tableFill: share of the page's row budget a table should use
keys.elements: evidence elements expected on an analytical page

geometryByFill.$comment: The geometric thresholds that move with fill, each set to a percentile of the corpus's own distribution over 2,125 rendered pages, so a floor can be read as a promise: an `airy` deck beats the emptiest 3% of published pages, a `balanced` deck the emptiest 10%, a `full` deck the emptiest quarter. The old ink ladder of 0.14 / 0.115 sat at the 36th and 26th percentiles - it rejected a third of the corpus, which is not a floor on emptiness but a floor on being denser than most published work. The dead band and column-void ceilings were already close to right (0.06 fires on 8% of published pages, 0.2 on 4%) and are unchanged; internal void at 0.16-0.32 fired on 1.3% and 0.6% and never caught anything, so it moves to the same 2-3% tail the others sit in. A page of type alone cannot reach ink_min at any honest length: see inkPerWord, which sets that page's floor instead.

inkPerWord.$comment: Ink a page of body type puts on the canvas, per word, measured by rendering text pages of 93 to 185 words at three and five points and reading the coverage back off the PNG. The relationship is linear: 95 words measured 0.0556, 128 words 0.0687, 185 words 0.0962. A text page's ink floor is this times the deck's own pageWords, so the ink a page must show is the ink its required words produce, and the two gates cannot disagree.

picture.$comment: A page whose evidence is a photograph carries fewer words, because the reader is looking at the subject rather than reading about it - and the body left for type is what sits beside or beneath the frame. So the word floor follows the geometry, exactly as inkPerWord makes a text page's ink floor follow its own word floor, rather than adding a second constant nobody measured: the floor is pageWords times the share of the body that is not photograph. shareMax caps the relief, so a page cannot buy its way out of carrying an argument by growing its picture; MISSING_ARGUMENT holds the other end and IMAGE_BUDGET caps how many pages may do this at all.

plan.$comment: Thresholds for the plan gates, which judge the dot-dash before a page is drawn. The mix bands and the entropy floor are calibrated on the example decks and are GUIDELINES - move them with judgement as real plans are measured against them. The shapes of the tests are not guidelines: charts and tables get separate bands because merging them into one 45% floor is what let a deck of 43% tables pass more comfortably than a balanced one.

mix.$comment: Measured over 237 published content pages, one per deck, by the family that dominates the page: chart 0.371, text 0.300, mixed 0.135, table 0.110, diagram 0.076, picture 0.008. The floors sit below what the corpus does so a real deck would pass; the caps sit above it. `picture` had a 0.05 FLOOR here, which asked for six times the photographs a published deck carries - pictures appear on 11.8% of pages, but almost always beside the evidence rather than as it. `text` had no band at all, which is why the composer never planned a page of type and then produced fifty pages of commentary restating the exhibit beside it: a third of published pages carry no exhibit at all.

craft.$comment: What the dot-dash has to record about the *craft* of a page, not only its evidence family. A generated 50-page deck passed every mix, entropy and anchor gate and still read as dry, because none of these were written down and so none were ever chosen: 10 tables with a median of 3 rows and not one treatment among them, 18 charts with not one annotation, 35 point lists with not one highlighted phrase. The floors used to be 0.20 and 0.25, guessed off four self-authored decks. Measured against 264 published pages they are 0.63 and 0.89: annotating the chart and treating the table is what these firms do almost every time, not a flourish a quarter of pages earn.

reference.$comment: Measured, not asserted. `slides` is the pixel sample: 2,125 pages from 426 published decks rendered onto the same 1280x720 canvas page_gates.py reads, with the same luminance cuts. `corpus` is the wide sample: every analytical page of every admitted landscape deck, 16,334 of them, measured off `pdftotext -bbox`. `judged` is a vision pass over 264 pages, one per deck, against evals/corpus/rubric.md. The previous version of this block claimed 137 hand-decomposed slides that nothing in the tree could reproduce; its wide word figures survived re-measurement almost exactly, its band split and its numeric token count did not.

exceedance.$comment: Share of the 2,125 rendered corpus pages each candidate threshold would flag.
